# 3D Fractal Multiverse PWA — Complete Technical & Publication Corpus
Canonical Dossier: https://steven.kleynenberg.com/pp/fract/
Live Google Cloud Deployment: https://fract.kleynenberg.com/
Featured Deeplink (Node 10, seed 452839): https://fract.kleynenberg.com/#uni=10&ft=10&seed=452839&x=0&y=0&z=0.49977559077972916&cs=0.2878
Static PWA Mirror: https://steven.kleynenberg.com/pp/fract/pwa/
Author: Steven Kleynenberg (Delft, South Holland, The Netherlands)
Contact: steven@kleynenberg.com

## 1. Software Architecture
- Monolithic zero-dependency WebGL 2.0 fragment shader engine rendering 13 complex dynamical archetypes (Mandelbrot Core, Douady's Rabbit, Feigenbaum Tip, and Julia nodes 1..12).
- Analytic perturbation theory (z_n + delta_n) with Decimal.js 50-digit reference precision to bypass IEEE 754 single-precision limits at zoom depths beyond 10^7.
- 3D CSS/WebGL barrier warp transitions at zoom < 5e-12 or zoom > 4.8 accompanied by procedural WebAudio oscillator synthesis.
- Multi-user Python aiohttp server (`server/fractal_server.py`, port 31415) synchronizing live sector coordinates over WebSockets.

## 2. Accompanying IEEEtran Manuscript (fractal.tex / fractal.pdf)
Title: Monolithic PWA Architectures and Real-Time Fractal Universes: Outperforming Hardware Constraints via Analytic Continuation and Sub-Pixel Blur Kernels
Authors: Steven Kleynenberg (Independent Researcher, Delft, Netherlands) and Google Gemini v3.5 (Artificial Intelligence Division, Google LLC)
Artifacts:
- PDF: https://steven.kleynenberg.com/pp/fract/server/latex/fractal.pdf
- LaTeX: https://steven.kleynenberg.com/pp/fract/server/latex/fractal.tex
Summary: Formalizes single-bundle PWA scientific visualization across three mathematical spaces (Analytic Mandelbrot Extension, Newton-Raphson Basins for Transcendental Polynomials, and Non-Euclidean Apollonian Gasket Projection) paired with two-pass separable Gaussian blur kernels and velocity-weighted temporal accumulation, sustaining 60 FPS up to 10^12 zoom depth (15.8 ms/frame vs 240.0 ms/frame for naive Float64).
